title: System.Windows.Forms.Timer / System.Timers.Timer with Thread.Sleep loops — replace with PeriodicTimer in .NET 10
notes: System.Windows.Forms.Timer is only available in the net10.0-windows TFM and requires a UI message pump — it cannot be used in ASP.NET Core or Worker Service projects. System.Timers.Timer is cross-platform but fires on ThreadPool threads without CancellationToken support, making graceful shutdown unreliable. Thread.Sleep loops block a thread and cannot be cancelled cleanly. In .NET 10, the idiomatic replacement for all three is PeriodicTimer combined with BackgroundService: `await using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10)); while (await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken)) { await ProcessBatch(stoppingToken); }`. The spec must capture the tick interval and whether the work is CPU-bound or I/O-bound, as PeriodicTimer coalesces missed ticks (no queue build-up) whereas some Framework timers do not.
